newsitem.title: USA: U.S. EPA hears comments on proposed Ariz. RFG plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. EPA hears comments on proposed Ariz. RFG plan.

text.p: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) heard comments from the public Tuesday on a proposed summer deadline to require cleaner-burning gasoline in the Phoenix area, an EPA spokesman said.
On July 1, the EPA hopes federal reformulated gasoline (RFG) becomes available at Phoenix gasoline stations.
"We'll be accepting public comments for 30 days," Randy Wittorp, an EPA spokesman, said after Tuesday's meeting.
Around 30 percent of gasoline sold in the U.S. is RFG.

The meeting, which lasted two hours, took place at Arizona's Department of Environmental Quality here and featured representives from environmental, government, and petroleum groups. Overall, speakers favored using RFG.
"A couple petroleum officials expressed that they needed more time to prepare to provide the fuel," Wittorp said.
After the public comment period, EPA officials hope to finalize the July deadline quickly.
Today's meeting resulted from a mid-January letter from the Arizona governor to EPA asking to join the cleaner fuel program.
Arizona, like a handful of U.S. cities and states, has volunteered to require RFG as part of a plan to improve air quality.
The Phoenix area has fallen out of compliance with national clean air standards in recent years, Wittorp said, with ground-level ozone exceeding federal limits several days out of the year.
